children: Athar shares his perspective on climate change at the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, joining young participants from six countries on the global stage.

ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Athar, a young student from Indonesia, took the stage at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, to share his thoughts on climate change and the future of the planet.

Speaking alongside young participants from Türkiye, China, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Thailand, Athar delivered his message in English, addressing the climate concerns, questions, and hopes of Indonesian children for a better environmental future. His participation demonstrated how children can use English to communicate their ideas and contribute to conversations that extend beyond their own communities.
Athar was among nine young participants from six countries supported by 51Talk, a global 1-on-1 online English education platform.
Since 2019, 51Talk has helped young learners share their perspectives at UN events, with COP31 marking the fifth time the company has brought young participants to speak on a UN stage.
Athar's Experience on the Global Stage
For Athar, 9, from Jakarta, participating in COP31 was an opportunity to speak about an issue that matters to him while experiencing what it means to address an international audience.

In his presentation, Athar shared his perspective on environmental responsibility, highlighting how small actions, such as reducing plastic waste and taking care of nature, can make a difference in protecting our planet. He encouraged listeners to take collective action for a healthier and more sustainable future for the next generation.

"I was a little nervous at first, but when I stood on the stage, I felt happy and proud. It was a great opportunity for me to share my thoughts and bring the perspectives of Indonesian children to the world," Athar said.

Ahead of the conference, Athar prepared for his speech through 51Talk's 1-on-1 online English lessons and dedicated speech practice, with support from his family. Working with his English teachers, he practiced organizing his thoughts and expressing his ideas clearly and confidently in English.

The experience also offered opportunities beyond public speaking. During his time in Antalya, Athar met young participants from different countries, exchanged ideas, and experienced firsthand how a shared language can bring people together.

"It was a special experience for me to meet people from different countries and share my thoughts about protecting our planet. I hope the questions I brought from Indonesian children can help more people listen to what children think about our future," Athar added.
Building Speaking Confidence Beyond the Classroom
At 51Talk, learning English is about more than developing language proficiency. It is also about helping children gain the confidence to express themselves and communicate in real-world situations.

51Talk combines personalized 1-on-1 online English lessons, structured curricula, and a global network of over 10,000 English teachers supported by professional training and teaching standards. Through interactive lessons and individualized guidance, children have regular opportunities to practice speaking, share opinions, and strengthen their communication skills.
Athar's participation at COP31 reflects this approach, showing how English learning can create opportunities for children to share their ideas on an international stage.

"Seeing Athar take part in COP31 is a proud moment for us. From his experience at the Global Youth Summit to this international climate conference, he continues to show that children can make meaningful contributions to important global conversations. We are glad to support his journey and see him take this opportunity to represent Indonesia," said Martin, General Manager of 51Talk Indonesia.

To further support practical communication skills, 51Talk introduced Global Communicator in 2026, a curriculum designed to connect English learning with real-world communication. Based on a syllabus licensed by Oxford University Press and developed by 51Talk, Global Communicator features immersive, task-based activities built around everyday situations and cross-cultural topics. AI-supported personalization and learning feedback help address individual learning needs and make progress more visible to families.
About 51Talk

Founded in 2011, 51Talk is a global 1-on-1 online English education platform for children aged 3 to 15. Through interactive lessons, structured curricula, and personalized instruction, 51Talk helps young learners build practical English communication skills and speaking confidence.
For more information, visit: https://www.51talk.com/id/index/
